result.topic_en: An addendum to §40 in Latin: for the case where the modulus of q equals unity, the formulas 1–7 (log K, log K', K, KK', etc.) are integrated with respect to q to give series of logarithms that remain convergent.
result.transcription:
Additamentum ad §$^{um}$. 40.
Formulae in hoc §$^{o}$ propositae, in eo casu, ubi modulus ipsius $q$ unitatem aequat[-ur-], consideratione satis dignae videntur, quippe quae functiones [-unius-] variabilis pro quovis [-valore-] argumenti valore discontinuas {+suppeditent+} [-praebeant-].
[-Primo in hunc finem formulas 1–7 integremus-]
[-48) $\int \log k \frac{dq}{q}$-] Series quidem propositae magna ex parte pro modulo ipsius $q$ unitati aequali non convergunt, sed integrando [-series-] series convergentes inde derivari possunt. Itaque primo integralia formularum 1–7 {+exhibemus+} [-proponemus-]
48) $\int_0 \left(\log k \frac{dq}{q} - \log 4\sqrt{q}\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\log(1+q) + \frac{4}{4}\log(1+q^2) - \frac{4}{9}\log(1+q^3) + \frac{4}{16}\log(1+q^4)$
49) $\int_0 -\log k' \frac{dq}{q} = 4\log\frac{1+q}{1-q} + \frac{4}{9}\log\frac{1+q^3}{1-q^3} + \frac{4}{25}\log\frac{1+q^5}{1-q^5}$
50) $\int_0 \log\frac{2K}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\cdot\log(1+q) + \frac{4}{9}\log(1+q^3) + \frac{4}{25}\log(1+q^5)$
51) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = [-4\log(1+q)-] - 4\log(1-q) + \frac{4}{3}\log(1-q^3) - \frac{4}{5}\log(1-q^5)$
$= + 2i\log\frac{1-qi}{1+qi} + \frac{2i}{2}\log\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} + \frac{2i}{3}\log\frac{1-q^3i}{1+q^3i}$
52) $\int_0 \frac{2kK}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\log\frac{1+\sqrt{q}}{1-\sqrt{q}} - \frac{4}{3}\log\frac{1+\sqrt{q^3}}{1-\sqrt{q^3}} + \frac{4}{5}\log\frac{1+\sqrt{q^5}}{1-\sqrt{q^5}}$
53) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2k'K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = [-4i-] 4i\log\frac{1-\sqrt{q}i}{1+\sqrt{q}i} + \frac{4i}{3}\log\frac{1-\sqrt{q^3}i}{1+\sqrt{q^3}i} + \frac{4i}{5}\log\frac{1-\sqrt{q^5}i}{1+\sqrt{q^5}i}$
$-\frac{4}{1}\log(1+q) + \frac{4}{3}\log(1+q^3) - \frac{4}{5}\log(1+q^5)$ [?]
$= -\frac{2i}{1}\log\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} + \frac{2i}{3}\log\frac{1-q^6i}{1+q^6i} - \frac{2i}{5}\log\frac{1-q^{10}i}{1+q^{10}i}$ [?]

items.quote: Formulae in hoc §$^{o}$ propositae, in eo casu, ubi modulus ipsius $q$ unitatem aequat[-ur-], consideratione satis dignae videntur, quippe quae functiones [-unius-] variabilis pro quovis [-valore-] argumenti valore discontinuas {+suppeditent+}
items.english: The formulas proposed in this section, in the case where the modulus of q equals unity, seem worthy of consideration, since they furnish functions of a variable that are discontinuous for every value of the argument.

items.quote: Series quidem propositae magna ex parte pro modulo ipsius $q$ unitati aequali non convergunt, sed integrando [-series-] series convergentes inde derivari possunt.
items.english: The proposed series for the most part do not converge when the modulus of q equals unity, but by integrating, convergent series can be derived from them.
Therefore we first exhibit the integrals of formulas 1–7.
